title: Enforce schema, required fields, tool permissions, and input contracts before semantic scoring while identifying requirements that structure alone cannot prove

questions.prompt:
A support agent can call two tools: `close_ticket(ticket_id, resolution)` and `escalate(ticket_id, reason)`. Before any tool runs, two deterministic checks execute:

1. a **permission check** that rejects any tool not on the agent's allowlist (the list of tools it may call; both tools above are on it), and
2. a **schema check** that rejects arguments that do not match that tool's JSON schema.

No other deterministic checks run.

In one test case, a customer reports a suspected account breach. Company policy says breach reports must be escalated. The agent calls `close_ticket` with a valid ticket ID and a non-empty resolution string. Both checks pass.

Explain why both deterministic checks passed even though the agent did the wrong thing.

rubric.point: The permission check only confirms that `close_ticket` is a tool the agent is allowed to call, which it is.
The schema check only confirms that the arguments have the required fields, types or shape, which they do.

Neither check encodes which permitted action this case required, so a structurally valid call to the wrong allowed tool passes; choosing `escalate` over `close_ticket` is a correctness decision that structure alone cannot prove.

questions.model: The permission check only asks whether `close_ticket` is on the allowlist, and it is. The schema check only asks whether the arguments are well formed, and they are. Neither check encodes which allowed action this case requires, so a structurally valid call to the wrong permitted tool passes both.

c1.text: it is agent decision failure, not deterministic check. agent correctly called a tool, with valid params, so deterministic checks are passed.

annotations.quote: agent correctly called a tool, with valid params, so deterministic checks are passed.
annotations.note: You note the call was valid, but you don't say what each check verifies. The permission check confirms the tool is allowlisted, and the schema check confirms the arguments are well formed.

annotations.quote: it is agent decision failure, not deterministic check.
annotations.note: You identified a decision failure, which is the right direction. You needed to explain that neither check encodes which permitted tool this case required, so picking `close_ticket` over `escalate` is a correctness question that structure can't prove.

c1.feedback: You correctly call it an agent decision failure, but you never explain what each check tests or why neither can tell that `escalate` was required.
